depositMissing.0: Card deposits normally credit within a few minutes. Bank transfers can take 1–3 business days depending on your bank, and crypto deposits credit after the required network confirmations.
depositMissing.1: You can check the current state of every payment under Transactions History — anything still processing shows as Pending there.

depositPending.0: A deposit stays Pending until the payment provider confirms settlement. Nothing is required from you while it is in that state.
depositPending.1: If a card deposit has been pending for more than 2 hours, or a bank transfer for more than 3 business days, an agent can trace it with your payment reference.

depositWrongAmount.0: If the credited amount differs from what you sent, the difference is usually the sending bank’s transfer fee or a currency conversion applied on their side.
depositWrongAmount.1: Send the payment confirmation from your bank to an agent and the account will be reconciled.

withdrawalTime.0: Withdrawals are processed back to the original funding method, as anti-money-laundering rules require. Requests submitted before the daily cut-off are reviewed the same business day.
withdrawalTime.1: Once approved, card refunds take 3–5 business days to appear, bank transfers 1–3 business days, and crypto withdrawals are sent once the network confirms.

withdrawalRejected.0: Withdrawals are most often declined for one of three reasons: verification is incomplete, the destination does not match the original funding method, or open positions would leave the account below its margin requirement.
withdrawalRejected.1: Check Settings → KYC Verification first — an unverified account cannot withdraw.

kyc.0: Verification needs a government ID, a proof of address dated within the last 3 months, and a selfie. Upload them under Settings → KYC Verification.
kyc.1: Documents are usually reviewed within one business day. Rejections are almost always a cropped edge, glare on the document, or an address document that is too old.

kycRejected.0: Re-upload using the Replace button on the rejected document. Photograph it flat, in daylight, with all four corners visible and no flash.
kycRejected.1: Utility bills, bank statements and council tax letters are accepted as proof of address. Mobile phone bills and handwritten documents are not.

marginCall.0: Positions are closed automatically when your margin level falls to the close-out threshold. This protects you from going into negative balance and happens without prior notice.
marginCall.1: You can reduce the risk by lowering position size, adding funds, or setting a Stop Loss that triggers before the close-out level is reached.

leverage.0: Your account leverage is shown on the order ticket next to the estimated margin. Higher leverage lowers the margin per position but makes a close-out happen sooner.
leverage.1: To apply for a higher tier, go to Settings → Documents → Leverage Increase Request. Requests are reviewed against your trading experience and account history.

charges.0: Three costs apply: the spread (the difference between the buy and sell price), commission where the instrument charges one, and overnight financing on positions held past the daily rollover.
charges.1: Overnight financing can be positive or negative depending on direction and instrument, and it is the cost most often mistaken for an unexplained deduction.

loginIssue.0: You can set a new password from Settings → My Profile → Change Password, or use Forgot password on the login screen.
loginIssue.1: If you are not receiving the reset email, check your spam folder and confirm you are using the address the account was opened with.
